Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2) shows a white arrow pointing to a distinct, well-circumscribed, lobulated mass in the right lower lung zone. This radiographic appearance is characteristic of a pulmonary nodule/mass consistent with primary lung carcinoma, which serves as the source for the metastasis described in the clinical scenario. Options describing breast masses or enhancement patterns are not visible on a plain radiograph, and other lung descriptions do not match the indicated lesion.
